correctness.rationale: A length-(n+1) word fixes two distinct consecutive n-arcs unless constant. Contracting the pair preserves vertex balance. H minus the intermediate vertex is weakly connected because a lower-order de Bruijn cycle supplies a Hamilton cycle on H vertices, leaving a spanning path after deletion. The contracted H is connected except when q=2, the intermediate vertex is constant, and the prescribed incoming and outgoing arcs are its two nonloops. Euler expansion proves the converse. Every boundary q=2,n=2 is included. The finite checker verified all 1,175 candidate inputs and independent binary full-cycle cases. These computations are verification only.

value.rationale: Exact complete support of next-order word distribution is an intrinsic invariant for uniformly sampled de Bruijn cycles. The theorem settles it for the entire infinite q,n family, identifies a genuine binary-only exceptional obstruction, and constructively characterizes which motifs can be enforced. Exact support is not automatic from de Bruijn cycle existence, count, or random generation; no arbitrary parameter slice was introduced.
